topics.title: How Washi is laid out
topics.how: The top bar has document tabs, the command search (Ctrl+K), the AI button, help, theme and settings. Under it the ribbon has tabs: Home, Comment, Edit, Pages, Forms, Protect, Convert. The left rail opens side panels: Pages (thumbnails), Bookmarks, Find, Comments, Attachments, Help. The status bar at the bottom has page navigation, zoom and page layout.

topics.title: Open a PDF
topics.how: Press Open on the start page or in the Home tab, or press Ctrl+O. You can also drag files into the window, or right-click a PDF in Explorer and choose Open with > Washi. XPS, EPUB and images are converted to PDF when opened.

topics.title: Save or save as
topics.how: Press Save (Ctrl+S) to write changes back to the file, or Save as (Ctrl+Shift+S) to make a new file. A red dot on a tab means it has unsaved changes.
topics.where: Home tab > Save, or the save icon at the right of the ribbon tabs

topics.title: Print
topics.how: Press Print in the Home tab or Ctrl+P. Washi prepares the pages including comments and opens the Windows print dialog.

topics.title: Read e-books (EPUB, MOBI, FB2)
topics.how: Open them like a PDF (Open, drag & drop, or Open with). Washi lays the book out on book-sized pages; its chapters appear as bookmarks and its links work. Change the letter size with Text size in the Home tab. You can highlight, comment, search and summarise with AI; Save as stores a PDF copy and the original e-book is never changed.
topics.where: Home tab > Open, Home tab > Text size

topics.title: Save a copy under another name or folder
topics.how: Press Save as in the Home tab (Ctrl+Shift+S) or right-click the document tab. If a file is in a protected folder such as Program Files, or open in another program, Washi explains why it can't save there and offers Save a copy as.

topics.title: Create a blank PDF
topics.how: On the start page press Blank PDF, or use Ctrl+N. Then add text with Add text (Edit tab) or insert pages from other files (Pages tab).

topics.title: Combine (merge) several files into one PDF
topics.how: Press Combine files on the start page or in the Convert tab and choose the files in the order you want. To add pages to the open document instead, use Pages tab > From file.

topics.title: Make a PDF from images or scans
topics.how: Press Images to PDF on the start page or From images in the Convert tab and choose the pictures. Each image becomes one page.

topics.title: Zoom and fit
topics.how: Use Ctrl + mouse wheel, Ctrl+plus / Ctrl+minus, or the zoom controls in the status bar. Fit width (Ctrl+2) and Fit page (Ctrl+0) size the page to the window; click the percentage for presets.

topics.title: Single page, continuous or two pages
topics.how: The three buttons at the right of the zoom controls in the status bar switch between continuous scrolling, one page at a time and two pages side by side (like a book).

topics.title: Go to a page
topics.how: Type a page number in the box in the status bar and press Enter (Ctrl+G jumps there). PgUp/PgDn, Home and End also work. Click a thumbnail in the Pages panel or a bookmark to jump.

topics.title: Find text
topics.how: Press Ctrl+F or the Find panel in the left rail, type the words, then press Enter for the next match (Shift+Enter for the previous one). Options: match case and whole words. Matches are highlighted on the pages.

topics.title: Page thumbnails
topics.how: The Pages panel in the left rail shows all pages. Click to jump, Ctrl+click or Shift+click to select several, drag to reorder, right-click for rotate, duplicate, extract or delete.

topics.title: Select and copy text
topics.how: With the Select tool (V) drag over text. A small bar appears: highlight, underline, strike out, copy, and on supported PCs AI explain or translate. Ctrl+C copies too.

topics.title: Move around with the hand
topics.how: Choose Hand (H) and drag the page, or hold the Space bar with any tool.

topics.title: Highlight text
topics.how: Choose Highlight (M) in the Home or Comment tab, pick a colour at the right end of the ribbon, then drag over text. Or select text with the Select tool and press the highlighter in the little bar. For pictures or scans use Area highlight.

topics.title: Underline, strike out or squiggly
topics.how: In the Comment tab choose Underline, Strike or Squiggly and drag over text.

topics.title: Add a sticky note (comment)
topics.how: Choose Note (N) and click on the page. Type the comment and press Save. Double-click any comment to read or change it.

topics.title: Add a text box comment
topics.how: Choose Text box (T), drag a box and type. Choose a fill colour at the right of the ribbon first if you like. Double-click a text box later to change the text.

topics.title: Draw rectangles, ellipses, lines and arrows
topics.how: In the Comment tab choose Rectangle (R), Ellipse (O), Line (L) or Arrow (A) and drag on the page. Hold Shift for squares, circles and straight lines. Colour, width and fill are at the right end of the ribbon.

topics.title: Draw freehand with the pen
topics.how: Choose Pen (P) in the Comment tab and draw. Strokes made within a second are joined into one drawing.

topics.title: Stamp the document (Approved, Draft…)
topics.how: Press Stamp (S) in the Comment tab, choose a stamp or type your own text, then click on the page. Stamps carry your name and the date.

topics.title: Move, recolour or delete a comment
topics.how: With the Select tool click a comment or shape. Drag it to move, drag the handles to resize, use the bar above it for colour, fill, width, opacity, comment text and delete. The Delete key removes it.

topics.title: See all comments
topics.how: Open Comments in the left rail. Filter by text, type or author; click one to jump to it, double-click to edit it.
topics.where: Left rail > Comments, or Comment tab > List

topics.title: Edit existing text
topics.how: Choose Edit text (E) in the Edit or Home tab. Lines light up as you hover; click one, change the words and press Enter. Size, font style and colour are in the small bar above it. Washi keeps the original font when it can, otherwise it uses a matching Windows font.

topics.title: Add new text to the page
topics.how: Choose Add text (X) in the Edit tab, click where it should go and type. Choose font, size, bold, italic and colour in the bar, then press Add or click elsewhere.

topics.title: Erase part of a page
topics.how: Choose Erase in the Edit tab and drag over the content. It is removed and the area becomes white.

topics.title: Insert an image or logo
topics.how: Press Image in the Edit tab, choose the picture, then click or drag on the page. You can also drag an image file from Explorer onto a page.

topics.title: Sign a PDF
topics.how: Press Sign in the Edit tab. Draw your signature, type it in a handwriting font, or use an image. Washi can remember it. Then click or drag where it should go; you can move or resize it afterwards with the Select tool. This is a visual signature, not a certificate-based digital signature.

topics.title: Add a link
topics.how: Choose Link in the Edit tab, drag over the area and enter a web address or a page number.

topics.title: Add a watermark
topics.how: Press Watermark in the Edit or Pages tab. Set the text, size, angle, colour and opacity, and which pages.

topics.title: Page numbers, header and footer
topics.how: Press Numbers in the Pages tab. Write the text with {page}, {pages}, {date} or {name}, choose the position and the pages.

topics.title: Rotate pages
topics.how: Select pages in the Pages panel (or stay on the current page) and press Left or Right in the Pages tab, or Ctrl+R.

topics.title: Delete pages
topics.how: Select pages in the Pages panel and press Delete in the Pages tab, or right-click a thumbnail > Delete.

topics.title: Reorder pages
topics.how: Open the Pages panel and drag thumbnails to their new place. Select several with Ctrl+click to move them together.

topics.title: Insert pages
topics.how: In the Pages tab press Blank page to add an empty page after the current one, or From file to insert pages of another PDF or image after the current page. Duplicate copies the selected pages.
topics.where: Pages tab > Blank page / From file

topics.title: Extract pages to a new PDF
topics.how: Select the pages in the Pages panel and press Extract in the Pages tab, then choose the file name.

topics.title: Split a PDF into several files
topics.how: Press Split in the Pages tab and choose every N pages, by bookmarks, or your own ranges like 1-3; 4-8.

topics.title: Crop pages
topics.how: Choose Crop in the Pages tab, drag the area to keep and choose this page, all pages or the selected ones. Uncrop restores the full page.

topics.title: Bookmarks (table of contents)
topics.how: Open Bookmarks in the left rail (Ctrl+B). Click to jump. Use the + button to bookmark the current page; double-click to rename; right-click to indent, outdent, re-point or delete.

topics.title: Fill in a form
topics.how: Fields of a fillable PDF are shown as light-blue boxes. Click and type, tick checkboxes and choose from dropdowns; save when done. For forms without fields use Add text.

topics.title: Create form fields
topics.how: In the Forms tab choose Text field, Checkbox or Dropdown and drag on the page, then name the field.

topics.title: Flatten comments and forms
topics.how: Press Flatten in the Comment or Forms tab. Comments, stamps, signatures and form fields become part of the page and can no longer be changed.

topics.title: Redact (black out) sensitive content
topics.how: In the Protect tab choose Redact and drag over text or images. Then press Apply: everything under the marks is permanently removed and replaced by black boxes. Save afterwards.

topics.title: Protect with a password
topics.how: Press Password in the Protect tab. Set a password to open, and/or an owner password with permissions (print, copy, comment, edit). It is applied (AES-256) when you save. Unlock removes protection on the next save.

topics.title: Document properties
topics.how: Press Properties (Ctrl+D) in the Protect or Edit tab to see file details and change the title, author, subject and keywords.

topics.title: Convert a PDF to Word, text, HTML or images
topics.how: In the Convert tab press Word, Text, Markdown, HTML or Images, choose the pages (and resolution for images) and where to save.

topics.title: Make the file smaller
topics.how: Press Optimise in the Convert tab and choose Light, Balanced or Strong. Images are resampled and the file is recompressed; save afterwards.

topics.title: Attachments inside a PDF
topics.how: Open Attachments in the left rail to see files embedded in the PDF, save them, remove them, or attach a new one with +.

topics.title: Undo and redo
topics.how: Ctrl+Z undoes the last change, Ctrl+Y redoes it. The buttons are in the Home tab and at the right of the ribbon tabs. Washi keeps the last 60 steps per document.

topics.title: Light and dark theme
topics.how: Press the moon / sun button in the top bar. In Settings choose System, Light or Dark, an accent colour, and whether pages should turn dark too (reading mode).

topics.title: Settings
topics.how: The gear in the top bar opens Settings: theme, accent colour, intro animation, your name for comments, default zoom, and the local AI options.

topics.title: Search for any command
topics.how: Press Ctrl+K (or the search box in the top bar) and type what you want to do, like 'rotate' or 'password'. Enter runs it. Type a number to jump to that page.

topics.title: Keyboard shortcuts
topics.how: Settings > About Washi > Keyboard shortcuts lists them all. Single letters pick tools: V select, H hand, M highlight, N note, T text box, E edit text, X add text, R rectangle, O ellipse, L line, A arrow, P pen, S stamp.

topics.title: Summarise a document with AI
topics.how: On PCs with a Ryzen AI NPU, press Summarise in the Home tab or open the AI panel (sparkle button, Ctrl+Shift+A) and choose Quick summary, Key points or Detailed summary. It runs locally on the NPU; nothing is uploaded.
topics.where: Top bar > AI, Home tab > Summarise

topics.title: Ask questions about the document
topics.how: Open the AI panel, stay on 'This document' and type a question. Answers cite pages like (p. 3); click a page reference to jump there.

topics.title: Explain or translate selected text with AI
topics.how: Select text with the Select tool; the little bar offers Explain and Translate, and the … button offers Simplify, Key points and Proofread.

topics.title: Why is there no AI button?
topics.how: Washi's assistant runs on an AMD Ryzen AI 300/400 or Ryzen AI Max NPU with the FastFlowLM engine. On other PCs the AI is turned off; every other feature works the same. Settings shows the reason.

topics.title: Make Washi the default PDF app
topics.how: Open Settings (gear) and press Make Washi the default PDF app. Windows opens its Default apps page for Washi: set it for .pdf. Or in Explorer right-click a PDF > Open with > Choose another app > Washi > Always.
